hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي  يَحْيَى  ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ   ، عَنْ  سَالِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ   ،  أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ بَاعَ غُلَامًا لَهُ بِثَمَانِ مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ ، وَبَاعَهُ بِالْبَرَاءَةِ ، فَقَالَ الَّذِي ابْتَاعَهُ لِعَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ : بِالْغُلَامِ دَاءٌ لَمْ تُسَمِّهِ لِي ، فَاخْتَصَمَا إِلَى عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ ، فَقَالَ الرَّجُلُ : بَاعَنِي عَبْدًا وَبِهِ دَاءٌ لَمْ يُسَمِّهِ ، وَقَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ : بِعْتُهُ بِالْبَرَاءَةِ ،  " فَقَضَى  عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عَفَّانَ   عَلَى عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ ، أَنْ يَحْلِفَ لَهُ لَقَدْ بَاعَهُ الْعَبْدَ ، وَمَا بِهِ دَاءٌ يَعْلَمُهُ " ، فَأَبَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ أَنْ يَحْلِفَ ، وَارْتَجَعَ الْعَبْدَ ، فَصَحَّ عِنْدَهُ ، فَبَاعَهُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ بِأَلْفٍ وَخَمْسِ مِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ  . قَالَ  مَالِك  :  الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا : أَنَّ كُلَّ مَنِ ابْتَاعَ وَلِيدَةً فَحَمَلَتْ ، أَوْ عَبْدًا فَأَعْتَقَهُ ، وَكُلَّ أَمْرٍ دَخَلَهُ الْفَوْتُ حَتَّى لَا يُسْتَطَاعَ رَدُّهُ ، فَقَامَتِ الْبَيِّنَةُ إِنَّهُ قَدْ كَانَ بِهِ عَيْبٌ عِنْدَ الَّذِي بَاعَهُ ، أَوْ عُلِمَ ذَلِكَ بِاعْتِرَافٍ مِنَ الْبَائِعِ أَوْ غَيْرِهِ ، فَإِنَّ الْعَبْدَ أَوِ الْوَلِيدَةَ يُقَوَّمُ وَبِهِ الْعَيْبُ الَّذِي كَانَ بِهِ يَوْمَ اشْتَرَاهُ ، فَيُرَدُّ مِنَ الثَّمَنِ قَدْرُ مَا بَيْنَ قِيمَتِهِ صَحِيحًا ، وَقِيمَتِهِ وَبِهِ ذَلِكَ الْعَيْبُ  . قَالَ  مَالِكٌ  :  الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا فِي الرَّجُلِ يَشْتَرِي الْعَبْدَ ، ثُمَّ يَظْهَرُ مِنْهُ عَلَى عَيْبٍ يَرُدُّهُ مِنْهُ ، وَقَدْ حَدَثَ بِهِ عِنْدَ الْمُشْتَرِي عَيْبٌ آخَرُ ، إِنَّهُ إِذَا كَانَ الْعَيْبُ الَّذِي حَدَثَ بِهِ مُفْسِدًا ، مِثْلُ الْقَطْعِ ، أَوِ الْعَوَرِ ، أَوْ مَا أَشْبَهَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْعُيُوبِ الْمُفْسِدَةِ ، فَإِنَّ الَّذِي اشْتَرَى الْعَبْدَ بِخَيْرِ النَّظَرَيْنِ ، إِنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُوضَعَ عَنْهُ مِنْ ثَمَنِ الْعَبْدِ ، بِقَدْرِ الْعَيْبِ الَّذِي كَانَ بِالْعَبْدِ يَوْمَ اشْتَرَاهُ ، وُضِعَ عَنْهُ ، وَإِنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يَغْرَمَ قَدْرَ مَا أَصَابَ الْعَبْدَ مِنَ الْعَيْبِ عِنْدَهُ ، ثُمَّ يَرُدُّ الْعَبْدَ ، فَذَلِكَ لَهُ ، وَإِنْ مَاتَ الْعَبْدُ عِنْدَ الَّذِي اشْتَرَاهُ ، أُقِيمَ الْعَبْدُ وَبِهِ الْعَيْبُ الَّذِي كَانَ بِهِ يَوْمَ اشْتَرَاهُ ، فَيُنْظَرُ كَمْ ثَمَنُهُ ؟ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ قِيمَةُ الْعَبْدِ يَوْمَ اشْتَرَاهُ بِغَيْرِ عَيْبٍ مِائَةَ دِينَارٍ ، وَقِيمَتُهُ يَوْمَ اشْتَرَاهُ وَبِهِ الْعَيْبُ ثَمَانُونَ دِينَارًا ، وُضِعَ عَنِ الْمُشْتَرِي مَا بَيْنَ الْقِيمَتَيْنِ ، وَإِنَّمَا تَكُونُ الْقِيمَةُ يَوْمَ اشْتُرِيَ الْعَبْدُ  . قَالَ  مَالِك  :  الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا : أَنَّ مَنْ رَدَّ وَلِيدَةً مِنْ عَيْبٍ وَجَدَهُ بِهَا ، وَكَانَ قَدْ أَصَابَهَا ، أَنَّهَا إِنْ كَانَتْ بِكْرًا فَعَلَيْهِ مَا نَقَصَ مِنْ ثَمَنِهَا ، وَإِنْ كَانَتْ ثَيِّبًا فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ فِي إِصَابَتِهِ إِيَّاهَا شَيْءٌ ، لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ ضَامِنًا لَهَا  . قَالَ  مَالِك  :  الْأَمْرُ الْمُجْتَمَعُ عَلَيْهِ عِنْدَنَا فِيمَنْ بَاعَ عَبْدًا ، أَوْ وَلِيدَةً ، أَوْ حَيَوَانًا بِالْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمِيرَاثِ ، أَوْ غَيْرِهِمْ : فَقَدْ بَرِئَ مِنْ كُلِّ عَيْبٍ فِيمَا بَاعَ ، إِلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلِمَ فِي ذَلِكَ عَيْبًا ، فَكَتَمَهُ ، فَإِنْ كَانَ عَلِمَ عَيْبًا فَكَتَمَهُ ، لَمْ تَنْفَعْهُ تَبْرِئَتُهُ ، وَكَانَ مَا بَاعَ مَرْدُودًا عَلَيْهِ  . قَالَ  مَالِك  فِي الْجَارِيَةِ تُبَاعُ بِالْجَارِيتَيْنِ ، ثُمَّ يُوجَدُ بِإِحْدَى الْجَارِيَتَيْنِ عَيْبٌ تُرَدُّ مِنْهُ ، قَالَ :  تُقَامُ الْجَارِيَةُ الَّتِي كَانَتْ قِيمَةَ الْجَارِيَتَيْنِ ، فَيُنْظَرُ كَمْ ثَمَنُهَا ، ثُمَّ تُقَامُ الْجَارِيتَانِ بِغَيْرِ الْعَيْبِ الَّذِي وُجِدَ بِإِحْدَاهُمَا ، تُقَامَانِ صَحِيحَتَيْنِ سَالِمَتَيْنِ ، ثُمَّ يُقْسَمُ ثَمَنُ الْجَارِيَةِ الَّتِي بِيعَتْ بِالْجَارِيتَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا بِقَدْرِ ثَمَنِهِمَا ، حَتَّى يَقَعَ عَلَى كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا حِصَّتُهَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ عَلَى الْمُرْتَفِعَةِ ، بِقَدْرِ ارْتِفَاعِهَا ، وَعَلَى الْأُخْرَى بِقَدْرِهَا ، ثُمَّ يُنْظَرُ إِلَى الَّتِي بِهَا الْعَيْبُ ، فَيُرَدُّ بِقَدْرِ الَّذِي وَقَعَ عَلَيْهَا مِنْ تِلْكَ الْحِصَّةِ ، إِنْ كَانَتْ كَثِيرَةً أَوْ قَلِيلَةً ، وَإِنَّمَا تَكُونُ قِيمَةُ الْجَارِيَتَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ يَوْمَ قَبْضِهِمَا  . قَالَ  مَالِكٌ  فِي الرَّجُلِ يَشْتَرِي الْعَبْدَ ، فَيُؤَاجِرُهُ بِالْإِجَارَةِ الْعَظِيمَةِ ، أَوِ الْغَلَّةِ الْقَلِيلَةِ ، ثُمَّ يَجِدُ بِهِ عَيْبًا يُرَدُّ مِنْهُ :  إِنَّهُ يَرُدُّهُ بِذَلِكَ الْعَيْبِ ، وَتَكُونُ لَهُ إِجَارَتُهُ وَغَلَّتُهُ ، وَهَذَا الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَمَاعَةُ بِبَلَدِنَا ، وَذَلِكَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلًا ابْتَاعَ عَبْدًا ، فَبَنَى لَهُ دَارًا قِيمَةُ بِنَائِهَا ثَمَنُ الْعَبْدِ أَضْعَافًا ، ثُمَّ وَجَدَ بِهِ عَيْبًا يُرَدُّ مِنْهُ رَدَّهُ ، وَلَا يُحْسَبُ لِلْعَبْدِ عَلَيْهِ إِجَارَةٌ فِيمَا عَمِلَ لَهُ ، فَكَذَلِكَ تَكُونُ لَهُ إِجَارَتُهُ إِذَا آجَرَهُ مِنْ غَيْرِهِ ، لِأَنَّهُ ضَامِنٌ لَهُ ، وَهَذَا الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا .  قَالَ  مَالِكٌ  :  الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا فِيمَنِ ابْتَاعَ رَقِيقًا فِي صَفْقَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ، فَوَجَدَ فِي ذَلِكَ الرَّقِيقِ عَبْدًا مَسْرُوقًا ، أَوْ وَجَدَ بِعَبْدٍ مِنْهُمْ عَيْبًا ، إِنَّهُ يُنْظَرُ فِيمَا وُجِدَ مَسْرُوقًا ، أَوْ وَجَدَ بِهِ عَيْبًا ، فَإِنْ كَانَ هُوَ وَجْهَ ذَلِكَ الرَّقِيقِ ، أَوْ أَكْثَرَهُ ثَمَنًا ، أَوْ مِنْ أَجْلِهِ اشْتَرَى ، وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْفَضْلُ فِيمَا يَرَى النَّاسُ ، كَانَ ذَلِكَ الْبَيْعُ مَرْدُودًا كُلُّهُ ، وَإِنْ كَانَ الَّذِي وُجِدَ مَسْرُوقًا ، أَوْ وُجِدَ بِهِ الْعَيْبُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الرَّقِيقِ فِي الشَّيْءِ الْيَسِيرِ مِنْهُ ، لَيْسَ هُوَ وَجْهَ ذَلِكَ الرَّقِيقِ ، وَلَا مِنْ أَجْلِهِ اشْتُرِيَ ، وَلَا فِيهِ الْفَضْلُ فِيمَا يَرَى النَّاسُ رُدَّ ذَلِكَ الَّذِي وُجِدَ بِهِ الْعَيْبُ ، أَوْ وُجِدَ مَسْرُوقًا بِعَيْنِهِ ، بِقَدْرِ قِيمَتِهِ مِنَ الثَّمَنِ الَّذِي اشْتَرَى بِهِ أُولَئِكَ الرَّقِيقَ  *
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Salim ibn Abdullah: That Abdullah ibn Umar sold a slave of his for eight hundred dirhams and sold him with a disclaimer (al-bara'ah). Then the one who bought him said to Abdullah ibn Umar: 'The slave has a disease that you did not name to me.' So they disputed before Uthman ibn Affan. The man said: 'He sold me a slave who has a disease that he did not name.' And Abdullah said: 'I sold him with a disclaimer.' So Uthman ibn Affan judged upon Abdullah ibn Umar that he should swear to him that he indeed sold the slave while there was no disease in him that he knew of. But Abdullah refused to swear and took back the slave. Then he (the slave) became well in his possession. So Abdullah sold him after that for one thousand five hundred dirhams.

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas -> Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari -> Salim ibn Abdullah -> Abdullah ibn Umar

potential_issues.issue: Multiple 'an (عَنْ) transmission terms used by Malik and Yahya ibn Sa'id
potential_issues.impact: While both Malik and Yahya ibn Sa'id are highly reliable narrators (Malik being Awthaq al-Nas), the use of 'an could theoretically indicate indirect transmission. However, given their exceptional reliability and the fact that this is from Malik's Muwatta with well-documented chains, this does not significantly impact authenticity.

potential_issues.issue: The hadith is mawquf (stops at the Companion level) - describes an incident involving Abdullah ibn Umar and Uthman ibn Affan
potential_issues.impact: This is not a statement from the Prophet ﷺ but rather a historical incident showing the practice of the Companions. It has historical value but is not a marfu' hadith.

potential_issues.issue: Transmission uses 'anna (أَنَّ) from Salim about Abdullah ibn Umar
potential_issues.impact: The 'anna form often indicates disconnection, but Salim ibn Abdullah is the son of Abdullah ibn Umar and would have direct knowledge of his father's affairs. This usage is acceptable in this context.

Topics: Incident of Abdullah ibn Umar selling a slave with a defect
Dispute resolution before Uthman ibn Affan
Refusal to take an oath and its consequences

hadiths.arabicText:
حَدَّثَنِي  يَحْيَى  ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنِ  ابْنِ شِهَابٍ   ، أَنَّ  عُبَيْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُتْبَةَ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ   أَخْبَرَهُ ،  أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ مَسْعُودٍ ابْتَاعَ جَارِيَةً مِنَ امْرَأَتِهِ  زَيْنَبَ الثَّقَفِيَّةِ  ، وَاشْتَرَطَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّكَ إِنْ بِعْتَهَا فَهِيَ لِي بِالثَّمَنِ الَّذِي تَبِيعُهَا بِهِ ، فَسَأَلَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ ، عَنْ ذَلِكَ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ، فَقَالَ  عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ    " لَا تَقْرَبْهَا ، وَفِيهَا شَرْطٌ لِأَحَدٍ "  * 
$1269  1272
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade selling what one does not possess.

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas -> Nafi' -> Abdullah ibn Umar -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'an (عَنْ) by Malik from Nafi'
potential_issues.impact: This is the famous 'Golden Chain' (Silsilat al-Dhahab): Malik from Nafi' from Ibn Umar. Despite the use of 'an, this chain is considered among the most authentic in hadith literature. Malik heard extensively from Nafi', and there is no doubt about the connection.

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'anna (أَنَّ) from Nafi' about Ibn Umar
potential_issues.impact: Nafi' was the freed slave and close companion of Ibn Umar for approximately 30 years. The use of 'anna here does not indicate disconnection; it is Nafi' reporting what he witnessed from Ibn Umar. This is standard usage in such contexts.

Topics: Sale of what one does not possess

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  نَافِعٍ   ،  عَنْ  عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ   ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ :  " لَا يَطَأُ الرَّجُلُ وَلِيدَةً إِلَّا وَلِيدَةً إِنْ شَاءَ بَاعَهَا ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ وَهَبَهَا ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ أَمْسَكَهَا ، وَإِنْ شَاءَ صَنَعَ بِهَا مَا شَاءَ "  . قَالَ  مَالِكٌ  فِيمَنِ اشْتَرَى جَارِيَةً عَلَى شَرْطِ أَنْ لَا يَبِيعَهَا ، وَلَا يَهَبَهَا ، أَوْ مَا أَشْبَهَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الشُّرُوطِ :  فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَنْبَغِي لِلْمُشْتَرِي أَنْ يَطَأَهَا ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَبِيعَهَا ، وَلَا أَنْ يَهَبَهَا ، فَإِنْ كَانَ لَا يَمْلِكُ ذَلِكَ مِنْهَا ، فَلَمْ يَمْلِكْهَا مِلْكًا تَامًّا ، لِأَنَّهُ قَدِ اسْتُثْنِيَ عَلَيْهِ فِيهَا مَا مَلَكَهُ بِيَدِ غَيْرِهِ ، فَإِذَا دَخَلَ هَذَا الشَّرْطُ لَمْ يَصْلُحْ ، وَكَانَ بَيْعًا مَكْرُوهًا  *
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Anas ibn Malik: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade the sale of fruits until they become clearly good. It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what is "until they become clearly good"?' He said: 'Until they become red.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do you see, if Allah prevents the fruit (from ripening), by what right would one of you take the wealth of his brother?'

narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi al-Andalusi

potential_issues.issue: Multiple uses of 'an (عَنْ) throughout the chain
potential_issues.impact: While 'an can indicate potential indirect transmission, all narrators in this chain are highly reliable. Malik narrating from Humayd is well-documented, and Humayd is famous for narrating from Anas ibn Malik. The chain is sound despite the transmission terms.

Topics: Sale of fruits before they ripen
Protection of commercial transactions from uncertainty
Definition of fruit maturity for sale

hadiths.arabicText:
حَدَّثَنِي  يَحْيَى  ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنِ  ابْنِ شِهَابٍ   ،  أَنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عَامِرٍ أَهْدَى لِعُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ جَارِيَةً ، وَلَهَا زَوْجٌ ابْتَاعَهَا  بِالْبَصْرَةِ  ، فَقَالَ  عُثْمَانُ   :  " لَا أَقْرَبُهَا حَتَّى يُفَارِقَهَا زَوْجُهَا " ، فَأَرْضَى ابْنُ عَامِرٍ زَوْجَهَا ، فَفَارَقَهَا  * 
$1271  1274   وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنِ  ابْنِ شِهَابٍ   ، عَنْ  أَبِي سَلَمَةَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ عَوْفٍ   ،  أَنَّ  عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ عَوْفٍ    " ابْتَاعَ وَلِيدَةً ، فَوَجَدَهَا ذَاتَ زَوْجٍ ، فَرَدَّهَا "  * 
"
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Ibn Abbas: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina while they were paying in advance for fruits for one, two, and three years. So he said: 'Whoever pays in advance for something, let him pay in advance for it in a known measure and a known weight, for a known term.'

potential_issues.issue: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri uses 'an (عَنْ) and he is classified as a mudallis (category 3 by some scholars, though others place him in category 2)
potential_issues.impact: Al-Zuhri is considered one of the most reliable narrators despite some classification as mudallis. His tadlis is minor and rarely affects the authenticity of his narrations, especially when narrating through Malik, who was extremely careful about whom he narrated from. This chain is considered authentic.

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'anna (أَنَّ) in two places in the chain
potential_issues.impact: The use of 'anna by Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr about Ibn Abbas could potentially indicate disconnection. However, the hadith is well-known and has support from other chains. The overall chain remains sound.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي  يَحْيَى  ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  نَافِعٍ   ،  عَنْ  عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ   ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ :  " مَنْ بَاعَ  نَخْلًا  قَدْ أُبِّرَتْ ، فَثَمَرُهَا لِلْبَائِعِ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشْتَرِطَ الْمُبْتَاعُ "  *
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Ibn Umar: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever buys food, let him not sell it until he takes possession of it.' Ibn Umar said: 'And we used to buy food in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he would send to us those who would forbid us from selling it in the place where we bought it until we moved it to the place where food was being sold.'

Movement of goods as condition for resale

hadiths.arabicText:
حَدَّثَنِي  يَحْيَى  ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  نَافِعٍ   ،  عَنِ  ابْنِ عُمَرَ   ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  " نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ الثِّمَارِ حَتَّى يَبْدُوَ صَلَاحُهَا ، نَهَى الْبَائِعَ وَالْمُشْتَرِيَ "  * 
$1274  1277
hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: 'The matters agreed upon among us is that whoever lends a loan to be paid at a term, then the debtor gives him a gift before paying his debt, or does something of service for him, it is not appropriate for him to take that, except what he used to do for him before the loan. If he used to give him a gift or do service for him before the debt, then there is no harm for him to take that. And likewise, it is disapproved that the debtor should give a gift to the creditor or provide him service after he pays his debt, if he did not use to do that for him before, because taking that is seeking to acquire through the debt more than what he lent, and that is an increase which he seeks from the debtor.'

narrators.name: Yahya
narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi al-Andalusi

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement (qawl) from Imam Malik himself, not a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This represents the scholarly consensus (ijma') as understood by Malik in Medina. It is mawquf at the level of the Tabi'i (not even reaching a Companion). This is valuable as legal opinion (fiqh) but not as a direct prophetic tradition.

potential_issues.issue: Not a marfu' hadith - no chain goes back to the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This is Malik's understanding of the principle of riba (usury) based on the general teachings, but it is not a direct statement from the Prophet ﷺ. Should be treated as juristic opinion rather than prophetic hadith.

Topics: Loans with benefit as form of usury
Gifts given in context of debt
Services rendered by debtor to creditor

hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  حُمَيْدٍ الطَّوِيلِ   ،  عَنْ  أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ   ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ " نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ الثِّمَارِ حَتَّى تُزْهِيَ " ، فَقِيلَ لَهُ : يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، وَمَا تُزْهِيَ ؟ فَقَالَ : " حِينَ تَحْمَرُّ " ، وَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ :  " أَرَأَيْتَ إِذَا مَنَعَ اللَّهُ الثَّمَرَةَ ، فَبِمَ يَأْخُذُ أَحَدُكُمْ مَالَ أَخِيهِ "  * 
$1275  1278
hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: 'The matters agreed upon among us concerning the two men who enter into a partnership with their wealth, then one of them separates and takes his share from the partnership before they finish their business, is that it is not permissible for him to take anything of the profit specifically unless they have looked at what they have, then they value what was sold with loss or profit, and they assess their goods at their current value. Then they separate based on that. This is what is done in our land regarding partnership.'

narrators.name: Yahya
narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi al-Andalusi

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement (qawl) from Imam Malik, not a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This represents the legal practice ('amal) of the people of Medina as understood by Malik. It is mawquf at the Tabi'i level. Valuable as juristic opinion (fiqh) and local custom, but not a direct prophetic tradition.

potential_issues.issue: Not a marfu' hadith - represents scholarly consensus in Medina
potential_issues.impact: This is Malik describing what 'the matters agreed upon among us' are, indicating it reflects the practice of the scholars of Medina rather than a direct statement from the Prophet ﷺ.

hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  أَبِي الرِّجَالِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ حَارِثَةَ   ، عَنْ أُمِّهِ  عَمْرَةَ بِنْتِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ   ،  أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ  " نَهَى عَنْ بَيْعِ الثِّمَارِ حَتَّى تَنْجُوَ مِنَ الْعَاهَةِ "  . قَالَ  مَالِكٌ  :  وَبَيْعُ الثِّمَارِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَبْدُوَ صَلَاحُهَا مِنْ بَيْعِ الْغَرَرِ  * 
$1276  1279
hadiths.english_translation: Malik said: 'The matters agreed upon among us is that there is no harm in taking a dinar for dirhams which you specify hand to hand, and taking dirhams for a dinar which you specify hand to hand. And there is no harm if some of it is delayed while most of it is received hand to hand, and the delayed portion is less than what was received immediately, whether the dirhams are for dinars or the dinars are for dirhams. But if most of the gold or silver is delayed and less is given immediately, then this is not appropriate. It is feared that this is mere delay for delay, because if one takes one dinar cash for two dinars on credit, or one dirham cash for two dirhams on credit, this is usurious delay, which is not disputed about.'

narrators.name: Yahya
narrators.full_name: Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi al-Andalusi

narrators.name: Malik
narrators.full_name: Malik ibn Anas ibn Malik ibn Abi Amir al-Asbahi

plainChains: Yahya ibn Yahya -> Malik ibn Anas

potential_issues.issue: This is a statement (qawl) from Imam Malik, not a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ
potential_issues.impact: This represents Malik's juristic reasoning on the principles of riba and currency exchange based on general prophetic guidance. It is mawquf at the Tabi'i level. Valuable as juristic opinion but not as direct prophetic tradition.

Topics: Currency exchange between gold and silver
Prevention of usury (riba) in currency transactions
Difference between permissible and impermissible credit

hadiths.arabicText:
وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ  مَالِك  ، عَنْ  أَبِي الزِّنَادِ   ، عَنْ  خَارِجَةَ بْنِ زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ   ،  عَنْ  زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ   " أَنَّهُ  كَانَ لَا يَبِيعُ ثِمَارَهُ ، حَتَّى تَطْلُعَ الثُّرَيَّا "  . قَالَ  مَالِكٌ  :  وَالْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا فِي بَيْعِ الْبِطِّيخِ ، وَالْقِثَّاءِ ، وَالْخِرْبِزِ ، وَالْجَزَرِ إِنَّ بَيْعَهُ إِذَا بَدَا صَلَاحُهُ حَلَالٌ جَائِزٌ ، ثُمَّ يَكُونُ لِلْمُشْتَرِي مَا يَنْبُتُ حَتَّى يَنْقَطِعَ ثَمَرُهُ وَيَهْلِكَ ، وَلَيْسَ فِي ذَلِكَ وَقْتٌ يُؤَقَّتُ ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ وَقْتَهُ مَعْرُوفٌ عِنْدَ النَّاسِ ، وَرُبَّمَا دَخَلَتْهُ الْعَاهَةُ ، فَقَطَعَتْ ثَمَرَتَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتُ ، فَإِذَا دَخَلَتْهُ الْعَاهَةُ بِجَائِحَةٍ تَبْلُغُ الثُّلُثَ فَصَاعِدًا ، كَانَ ذَلِكَ مَوْضُوعًا عَنِ الَّذِي ابْتَاعَهُ  * 
!
hadiths.english_translation: Narrated from Abu Hurayrah: That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade two sales in one sale.

potential_issues.issue: Multiple uses of 'an (عَنْ) throughout the chain
potential_issues.impact: Despite multiple 'an terms, this is a well-known chain. Malik from Abu al-Zinad from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah is a famous and authentic chain. All narrators are highly reliable and their connections are well-documented.

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'anna (أَنَّ) from A'raj about Abu Hurayrah
potential_issues.impact: Al-A'raj was a well-known student of Abu Hurayrah and frequently narrated from him. The use of 'anna here is standard and does not indicate disconnection.
